description: Map of where GenAI work sits (decision D-015): six stack layers plus four cross-cutting planes. Roles carry a work footprint (data/role_scores.json, field stack), skill categories map to layers here, and specialisations name the work that happens inside canonical roles. Rendered by scripts/build_role_map.py and scripts/build_role_hubs.py.
basis: Layer names and order follow the legacy handbook's six-layer stack (structure only, decision D-016); the definitions, planes, footprints and specialisations are this repository's, drawn from the role definitions in career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §3. Footprints are judgement (Grade D).
not_a_pay_model: Pay tracks employer tier and seniority, not application versus infrastructure work [B · T0-03 KF1]; the role rankings rejected the claim that GPU and inference roles have the highest pay ceilings. No pay, demand or value-capture figure is published per layer.

L6.name: Applications and deployment
L6.covers: AI features and products, deployment into customer environments, solution architecture, AI-native user experience

L5.name: Orchestration and context
L5.covers: agents and tool use, retrieval and RAG, agent protocols (MCP, A2A), memory and context pipelines

L4.name: Post-training and adaptation
L4.covers: fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning, domain adaptation, model-level evaluation, human data for training

L3.name: Inference and ML platforms
L3.covers: serving engines and their optimisation, gateways and routing, MLOps and LLMOps platforms, observability

L2.name: Foundation models and research
L2.covers: pre-training, architectures and scaling, interpretability, new methods at frontier labs

L1.name: Compute and hardware
L1.covers: accelerators, GPU kernels and compilers, clusters, interconnects and storage, capacity and reliability

evaluation.name: Evaluation and quality
evaluation.covers: measuring whether AI systems work at every layer: eval harnesses, golden sets, judge calibration, regression gates, online monitoring

assurance.name: Security, safety and governance
assurance.covers: security and red-teaming, responsible-AI controls, risk, audit and regulatory compliance

product.name: Product and strategy
product.covers: product outcomes for probabilistic systems: scoping, success metrics, economics, pilots

leadership.name: Leadership and independent practice
leadership.covers: leading AI teams and organisations, or practising independently as a consultant or fractional leader
